day_summary: SUNDAY RECOVERY — BTC REFERENCE CLOSE $63,439.36 (+$780.63 / +1.25% FROM AUGUST 1): STEP-ASIDE GAP NARROWS FOR FIRST TIME IN 4 SESSIONS TO $1,560.64 — STILL UNMET BUT CONSTRUCTIVE. SESSION OPENED NEAR THE AUGUST 1 REFERENCE CLOSE (~$62,659), HIT AN OVERNIGHT LOW OF $62,721.36 DURING THE LATE SATURDAY US HOURS / EARLY SUNDAY UTC TRANSITION, THEN STAGED A DECISIVE RECOVERY AT 02:00 UTC WHEN AGGRESSIVE BUYING DROVE BTC FROM $62,897 TO $63,501 (+$604) ON THE DAY'S HIGHEST-VOLUME CANDLE (215 BTC / ~$13.6M ON CRYPTO.COM). THE SESSION THEN TRADED IN A NARROW $63,000–$63,200 BAND THROUGH EUROPEAN AND EARLY US HOURS (08:00–17:00 UTC), ABSORBING A PULLBACK FROM THE OVERNIGHT HIGH. AN AFTERNOON RECOVERY TO $63,319 AT 18:00 UTC AND $63,399 AT 19:00 UTC LIFTED THE REFERENCE CLOSE TO $63,439.36, BRINGING THE STEP-ASIDE FRAMEWORK GAP DOWN TO $1,560.64 — THE FIRST NARROWING SINCE THE EXPIRY-DAY SELLOFF ON JULY 31 THAT BLEW THE GAP FROM $226.70 TO $2,038.01. AFTER THE REFERENCE CLOSE, BTC CONTINUED HIGHER TO $63,727 BY 21:45 UTC. THE STEP-ASIDE FRAMEWORK CONDITIONS REMAIN: (1) REFERENCE CLOSE $63,439.36 IS $1,560.64 BELOW THE $65,000 THRESHOLD — GAP NARROWED FROM $2,341.27 ON AUGUST 1 (FIRST IMPROVEMENT IN 4 SESSIONS); (2) ETF FLOWS: SPOT ETFS DO NOT TRADE ON WEEKENDS — FRIDAY JULY 31 CONFIRMED AT +$233M (IBIT $183M = 79%); MONDAY AUGUST 3 WILL BE THE FIRST NEW ETF DATA POINT. MACRO CALENDAR THIS WEEK: MONDAY AUGUST 3 BRINGS ISM MANUFACTURING PMI (9:45 AM ET) AND CONSTRUCTION SPENDING (10:00 AM ET) — THE WEEK'S FIRST MACRO CATALYST AHEAD OF ADP (AUG 5) AND NFP (AUG 7). SECURITY HEADWIND: A COLDCARD HARDWARE WALLET FIRMWARE FLAW DRAINED $70M FROM 1,196 WALLETS IN 41 MINUTES ON JULY 30 — A PRNG SUBSTITUTION ERROR IN MARCH 2021 FIRMWARE MADE SEED PHRASES COMPUTATIONALLY ENUMERABLE; SECURITY FIRMS WARN MORE WALLETS MAY BE AFFECTED, ADDING A RETAIL-CONFIDENCE HEADWIND ENTERING AUGUST.

extra.label: Coldcard $70M hardware wallet hack (July 30, 2026): firmware PRNG flaw drained 1,196 wallets in 41 minutes — retail confidence headwind entering August
extra.value: A major security incident surfaced: a firmware flaw in certain Coldcard hardware wallets (a March 2021 firmware integration error that routed seed generation to a software PRNG instead of the STM32 hardware RNG) made seed phrases computationally enumerable. Attackers drained $70M from 1,196 wallets in 41 minutes without ever touching the physical devices. CoinDesk, The Hacker News, and 247 Wall St. covered the incident on August 1. Security firms warn that more wallets may be at risk as owners cannot reliably determine if their device's seed was generated on vulnerable firmware. Hardware wallet security is foundational to self-custody adoption — this is a retail-confidence headwind entering the new week.

analysis:
## Technical analysis

### Session overview — Sunday recovery narrows step-aside gap for first time in 4 sessions

August 2, 2026 was BTC's second consecutive weekend post-expiry session. The pattern: (1) an overnight dip to the session low ($62,721.36 from the late Saturday US night / early Sunday UTC transition); (2) a decisive recovery surge at 02:00 UTC from $62,897 to $63,501 on the day's highest-volume candle (215 BTC / ~$13.6M on Crypto.com); and (3) a morning pullback to $62,972 (11:00 UTC) followed by a sustained afternoon recovery to close the 20:00 UTC reference window at $63,439.36. Total Crypto.com volume was approximately 1,088 BTC (~$68.8M) — modestly above Saturday's 764 BTC (~$48M) but well below any weekday session.

### Trend — first reference close improvement in 4 sessions; still below all major moving averages

BTC's reference close sequence over the step-aside period:
- July 24 (~$65,000): step-aside activated
- July 30 ($64,773.30): gap $226.70 — closest approach to re-entry
- July 31 ($62,961.99): gap $2,038.01 — expiry-day selloff
- August 1 ($62,658.73): gap $2,341.27 — further widening
- August 2 ($63,439.36): gap $1,560.64 — FIRST NARROWING

Today's improvement reverses the three-session widening trend, but does not change the broader technical structure. BTC remains below all four major moving averages (Intellectia.ai, CoinPedia, CCN consensus):
- 20-day EMA: ~$64,288 (nearest overhead MA; $849 above today's reference close)
- 50-day EMA: ~$64,891 (most-watched by active traders; $1,452 above today's close)
- 100-day EMA: ~$67,604 ($4,165 above)
- 200-day EMA: ~$73,308 ($9,869 above)

BTC has not traded above the 20-day EMA since the step-aside activation. The layered MA resistance from $64,288 to $73,308 means the path to re-entry passes through a dense overhead supply zone. A sustained recovery toward $65,000 requires clearing the 20d EMA ($64,288) and 50d EMA ($64,891) sequentially.

### Volume — the 02:00 UTC candle is the signal; total session remains thin Sunday

The session's total Crypto.com volume of 1,088 BTC (~$68.8M) reflects another thin weekend day. Volume was NOT evenly distributed: the 02:00 UTC candle alone accounted for approximately 215 BTC ($13.6M) — approximately 20% of the entire session volume — in a single hour. For comparison, the session average was ~44 BTC per candle.

Key volume interpretation: The 02:00 UTC surge on the day's highest-volume candle represents active buyers stepping in at the $62,897 level rather than organic drift. The fact that BTC subsequently held above $62,972 (the 11:00 UTC morning pullback low) and did not return to the overnight low ($62,721) suggests the 02:00 UTC buyers established a higher floor. This must be confirmed on weekday volume (10–30× higher than Sunday) starting Monday August 3.

Volume divergence note: Today's recovery (+1.25% reference close change) came on higher-than-Saturday volume — a mild bullish signal (rising price on rising relative volume). Contrast with August 1, where a small decline (−0.48%) came on even lighter volume. Both the price and volume trends are constructive on the weekend, but thin absolute volumes limit the interpretive confidence.

### Momentum — higher low + higher reference close; Asian session spike sets the week's reference

The hourly candle structure for August 2:
1. Overnight low ($62,721–$62,753): established in the late Saturday US night / early Sunday UTC period
2. 02:00 UTC decisive surge: highest-volume candle of the weekend; $62,897 → $63,501
3. 04:00–05:00 UTC: session high $63,566–$63,576 (Asian session peak)
4. 08:00–11:00 UTC: pullback to $62,972 (European session; lower high formation)
5. 12:00–16:00 UTC: $63,000–$63,200 consolidation floor (demand resets here)
6. 17:00–20:00 UTC: afternoon recovery to $63,439 reference close
7. 21:00 UTC (after reference close): further push to $63,727

The structure of higher low ($62,721 overnight → $62,972 morning pullback) and higher reference close ($62,659 Aug 1 → $63,439 Aug 2) is constructive. The afternoon recovery from the $63,000–$63,200 consolidation zone suggests buyers are defending this level ahead of the Monday open.

### ★ Strongest support — $63,000–$63,200 (afternoon demand floor)

The $63,000–$63,200 zone held as support across five hours of the afternoon session (12:00–16:00 UTC). Candle closes within this range:
- 12:00 UTC: close $63,071.81
- 13:00 UTC: close $63,065.99
- 14:00 UTC: close $63,018.63
- 15:00 UTC: close $63,054.00
- 16:00 UTC: open $63,054.01, close $63,126.98

Five consecutive hourly closes within a $100 range ($63,000–$63,100) indicate genuine demand equilibrium. Buyers stepped in here after the European session pullback from the 05:00 UTC high and prevented a return to overnight lows. The zone aligns with the lower boundary of the consensus technical support band ($63,000–$63,800 per Intellectia.ai).

Evidence summary: (1) Five consecutive hourly candle closes in a $100 band; (2) Buyers prevented a return to the $62,721–$62,753 overnight low; (3) Aligns with analyst consensus support band; (4) Zone was reclaimed from below after the 11:00 UTC low at $62,972. ### ★ Strongest resistance — $65,000 (framework threshold + dense EMA cluster)

$65,000 has now been rejected on a reference-close basis for seven consecutive sessions (July 24 through August 2). Evidence:
1. **Seven consecutive reference closes below $65,000** — including two intraday penetrations (July 30 high $65,186, July 31 high $65,411) that were immediately sold back below the threshold
2. **Dense EMA cluster overhead**: 20d EMA ($64,288) and 50d EMA ($64,891) form a $603 overhead resistance band that BTC must clear before reaching $65,000; each EMA is a potential rejection point for any recovery rally
3. **Options market structure**: dominant August positioning is the $60,000 put (bearish), not $65,000+ calls; this reflects market-maker supply above $65,000 and structural put demand below
4. **Framework self-reference**: the $65,000 level is the decision point — a reference close above it (combined with positive ETF flows) triggers re-entry; this creates a structural resistance as step-aside traders who re-enter at size absorb rally momentum

### Decision points for the week ahead

**1. Monday open vs. $63,000–$63,200 afternoon support**
The first test of today's Sunday recovery: can BTC maintain the $63,000–$63,200 zone on Monday's heavier institutional volume? A breach below $63,000 on a sustained weekday close suggests the Sunday recovery was a thin-volume counter-trend move. A hold above $63,200 validates the bid structure and sets up a push toward the 20-day EMA ($64,288).

**2. Monday August 3 ISM Manufacturing PMI (9:45 AM ET)**
The first macro signal of NFP week. A sub-50 reading (manufacturing contraction) reduces rate-hike expectations and weakens the dollar — a BTC positive. A surprise above 50 with firm prices component could revive September rate hike bets and push BTC back toward the $62,721–$62,753 overnight low zone.

**3. Monday ETF flow data (first post-weekend reading)**
The July 31 +$233M IBIT-led inflow needs confirmation. Two consecutive days of positive ETF flows would begin addressing Condition 2 of the step-aside framework — though Condition 1 ($65,000 reference close) remains the binding constraint. A single positive day, however large, is not enough to confirm a trend after July's record-low monthly total.

**4. August 7 NFP (8:30 AM ET)**
The single most important catalyst of the week. A soft reading (below 100K payrolls, rising unemployment) could simultaneously drive BTC toward $65,000 (Condition 1) and catalyze ETF inflows (Condition 2) — the first scenario where both framework conditions could converge within a week. A hot reading makes the $60,000 put trade the favored risk/reward and likely re-expands the step-aside gap.

### What invalidates the read

The step-aside framework is invalidated (re-entry triggered) only if a reference close above $65,000 coincides with confirmed positive ETF flows on the SAME date. Requirements:
- BTC 20:00 UTC reference close > $65,000 (currently 2.46% away from $63,439)
- Positive net ETF flows confirmed for the same calendar day
- Both conditions must be simultaneously met — neither alone triggers re-entry

Today's gap narrowing ($1,561 from threshold) is constructive but not definitive. The gap has closed and re-opened before (July 30 gap was just $226.70 before the July 31 expiry selloff immediately re-expanded it to $2,038). The earliest realistic convergence window is NFP week (August 7–8), and only if both the macro and flow readings align favorably. A Monday ISM surprise or ETF flow disappointment could re-expand the gap before NFP even arrives.
